14.headline: Kimi Antonelli turned a well-timed VSC into a fourth-straight-style stroll at F1's processional Madring debut, leaving pole-sitter Lando Norris third and the title all but decided.

bullets.text: **Antonelli** never had to make a pass to win: the virtual safety car for Lance Stroll's lap-12 retirement fell at the perfect moment for him and a moment too late for Norris, whose stop a lap later was also slow. He called it his least remarkable victory of the year and said he felt for Norris, who he thought deserved it.

**Norris** produced what he rated the best qualifying lap of his career — Andrea Stella called the bulk of it "a masterpiece" despite a scruffy final corner — to beat Antonelli to pole by 0.011s, then lost the race purely to VSC timing before clipping the Turn 7 wall.

**McLaren**'s weekend was doubly poor: Piastri was off the pace all through qualifying, picked up front wing damage in a lap-one clash with Russell, and was then left stuck in a midfield train behind Bortoleto and Colapinto after the team pitted him knowing that was a risk.

**Hamilton** was ahead of Verstappen off the line and looked a podium contender before a long brake pedal and a brake malfunction ended his race on lap six — after which he publicly conceded the title, saying Antonelli and Mercedes deserved it, with Ferrari's cushion over McLaren for second in the constructors' now 52 points.

**The Madring** drew praise as a qualifying challenge but delivered almost no on-track passing — Lawson on Colapinto and Russell on Lawson were the notable exceptions — and circuit chiefs have already confirmed revisions to the Turn 5/6 chicane, Turn 13 and Turn 20 for 2027; those changes had been proposed before this year's race but were shelved to avoid homologation and construction delays.

**Pirelli** defended the C2/C3/C4 allocation after Friday's heavy degradation evaporated into a routine one-stopper — Gasly ran his starting set to the penultimate lap before his mandatory change — arguing softer rubber would only have produced a tyre-management race given the roughly 25-second pitlane loss, one of the longest of the season.

**Colapinto** led the midfield home in seventh, holding off a quicker Piastri, and credited his qualifying execution to what he learned from Gasly's Monza pole lap; Alpine's deficit to Racing Bulls in the fight for fifth is down to nine points.

Away from the track, FIA president Mohammed Ben Sulayem has been discussing extra assistance for **Honda** with Fernando Alonso and Lawrence Stroll, with Mercedes and Red Bull said to be receptive, while Laurent Mekies admitted Red Bull's unexplained in-race car performance degradation is still unsolved and likely to run into next season.

quotes.speaker: Lewis Hamilton
quotes.quote: There's no stopping him and Mercedes this year

quotes.speaker: Oscar Piastri
quotes.quote: The medium tyre was just awful. It was good for literally one lap, but then it was terrible.

quotes.speaker: Charles Leclerc
quotes.quote: But in the race, there are some corners and it doesn't require a big change, I think just a small change or two small changes could change significantly the racing that we have.

quotes.speaker: Fernando Alonso
quotes.quote: The engine was very bad today
